speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the mechanism of the rear-end collision and whether you felt your leg snap into an outward, rotated position at the time of impact? I need to know if you are currently able to bear any weight on that right leg.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does moving your right leg in any direction significantly worsen the pain in your groin? I need to determine if there is any instability or mechanical locking in the joint.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The physical presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg is classic for a posterior hip dislocation. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray

text: The X-ray confirms a posterior hip dislocation of the right hip. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate closed reduction to prevent avascular necrosis of the femoral head. I will proceed with arranging urgent orthopedic consultation for reduction under anesthesia.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background information. Since the diagnosis is confirmed and urgent reduction is the priority, I will now coordinate with the orthopedic team immediately to proceed with the closed reduction under anesthesia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior hip dislocation
